info.title: X2KNWLDG local API — v1
info.summary: The frozen read-only HTTP contract of the Knowledge Canvas local web layer.
info.description:
Freezes canvas plan §15 (T-005). The API is a **reader**. Every response body is a record the adapters in `src/x2knwldg/adapters/` already produce from canonical files under `output/<source-id>/`, wrapped in a versioned envelope — this document defines no second shape for anything the index model already describes, and `$ref`s `schemas/v1/` rather than restating it.

Four rules the server may not break:

1. **Status is copied, never computed.** Every status in a response is the `Source.status` block verbatim, `UNKNOWN` included. The API has no more right to compute a run status than the UI does (ADR 0001 invariant 2).
2. **A missing artifact is reported, never masked.** An artifact absent at index time carries `available: false`, and `/api/media` answers `404 unavailable`. No placeholder, no fabricated bytes (canvas plan §15).
3. **An externally supplied id is resolved, never sanitised.** Every path parameter that names a run goes through `pipeline.resolve_run_dir`, which rejects rather than rewrites (D-020, risk R14). A malformed id is `400 invalid_id`; a well-formed id with nothing behind it is `404 not_found`.
4. **v1 is read-only.** There is no endpoint that writes to `output/`, and none at all that writes to `output/<id>/raw/`, which is immutable evidence (ADR 0001 invariant 1). Board persistence is Phase 3 and is deliberately not frozen here (D-027).

Loopback-only binding, path-traversal hardening, and range requests are `T-108`; they are operational obligations that this document states but cannot enforce.

Three facts about the **served** surface that this document deliberately does not declare as paths or operations. They are written down here so that a reader of the contract is not left to discover them from a running server:

1. **`GET /api/openapi.json` is served, and is not one of the paths below.** It returns this document byte for byte, with an `ETag` and a `304` on revalidation. It is excluded because a contract that declared the request for itself would describe its own retrieval as part of the surface it describes. The exclusion is asserted rather than assumed: `test_the_served_surface_is_exactly_the_frozen_one` walks the real router and compares what it finds against these paths *plus that one*, so a route added with `include_in_schema=False`, or any mount, fails the guard.
2. **`HEAD` is answered on every path below and declares no `head` operation.** RFC 9110 defines `HEAD` as `GET` without a body, so it needs no second declaration; one ASGI middleware honours it for every route, and the `Content-Length`, `Content-Range` and `Accept-Ranges` a `HEAD` carries are exactly the ones its `GET` would have carried — range probes included. A reader who sees only the declared `405` should read this sentence rather than conclude the method is refused.
3. **`GET /api/status` declares `503` and cannot raise it itself.** `status()` reports an unbuilt index as the state `absent` rather than refusing, precisely so that a UI can tell 'never indexed' from 'the server is broken'. The `503` stays declared because it stays reachable: a repository that fails while being asked what it is renders through the shared handler, on this path as on every other.

servers.description: Loopback only. The server must not bind a non-loopback interface (T-108). The port is an operational default that T-116 settles; it is not part of the frozen contract.

get.description: Reports what the index contains and when it was built. `sources_by_status` counts copied statuses; it never re-derives one, and a source whose validator file is missing is counted under `UNKNOWN` rather than folded into `PASS`.
One page of `Source` records. `status` filters on the copied validation status, so filtering for `PASS` cannot silently include a `PARTIAL` run.

The `Source` record together with the `Artifact` records it names in `artifact_ids`. The artifacts are embedded because the Reader needs them on first paint, not because they are a different shape from `/api/artifacts/{artifact_id}` — they are the same records.

get.summary: The knowledge units of one source
get.description: One page of `EntityRef` records belonging to *source_id*. In v1 these are knowledge units only: captions, segments, and coverage windows are reserved in the vocabulary and deliberately unemitted (D-023).
One page of `IndexedRelation` records whose `source_id` is *source_id*. Cross-source `expresses_concept` edges have a null `source_id` and are therefore reached through `/api/graph`, not here.
An `EntityRef` addressed by its three-part global id (D-011). A canonical concept is addressed as `library:concepts:<hash>` (D-016).

The `Artifact` record — what the file is, where it sits, whether it was present at index time. It is metadata about the file, never the file. Bytes come from `/api/media/{artifact_id}`. An artifact that was absent at index time is returned with `available: false` and a `200`: its record exists and the honest answer is that the file does not.

The byte channel for every artifact, canonical JSON and the Markdown report included — the API serves the file as written and never reinterprets, reformats, or summarises canonical content.

Read-only in every case. `raw/` artifacts are served but carry `immutable: true` and have no write endpoint in any version (ADR 0001 invariant 1). An `external` artifact — a YouTube video — has no bytes here: it answers `404 unavailable`, and the client uses `Artifact.url` (canvas plan §15: never assume a local media file exists).

Range requests are supported (T-108).

Conditional requests are supported. Every `200` and `206` carries a strong `ETag`, a `Last-Modified` and `Cache-Control: no-cache` — store it, but revalidate before reusing it, because a canonical file is rewritten by a re-ingest and no server can promise a lifetime for that. A client that already holds the representation revalidates with `If-None-Match` (or `If-Modified-Since`) and is answered `304`. A `Range` may be guarded with `If-Range`; when the guard does not match, the range is ignored and the whole representation is sent.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Byte range, per RFC 9110. Answered with 206 and a Content-Range header.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Entity tags the client already holds. Compared with the **weak** comparison function of RFC 9110 §13.1.2, so `W/"…"` matches `"…"`; a comma-separated list and `*` are both honoured. A match is `304`, and outranks `Range`.

parameters.name: If-Modified-Since
parameters.description: HTTP-date of the client's copy. Consulted only when there is no `If-None-Match`, which is the precedence RFC 9110 §13.2.2 fixes. An unparseable date is ignored rather than refused.

parameters.name: If-Range
parameters.description: Guards the `Range`: an entity tag, compared **strongly** so a `W/` tag never matches, or the exact `Last-Modified` date. When it does not match, the `Range` is ignored and the whole representation is sent with `200` — never `416`.

200.description:
The whole artifact. `Content-Type` is `Artifact.media_type` when one is registered, and `application/octet-stream` when it is not — a media type is stated, never guessed.

It is also **allowlisted**, which the earlier wording did not say: a registered type outside the set this channel serves — the adapters' own table, plus the whole `audio/`, `video/` and `image/` families, less `image/svg+xml` — is answered `404 unavailable` rather than sent. The UI is served from `/` on this same origin, so a record stating `text/html` would otherwise run there. Such a record is a damaged one; refusing it is not the same as guessing a replacement for it.

Content-Length.description: Bytes in the body: the whole artifact on a `200`, the range's length on a `206`.

X-Content-Type-Options.description: `nosniff`. The UI is served from `/` on this same origin, so a sniffed type would decide what a document *runs as*.

ETag.description: A strong entity tag for the bytes on disk. Strong because `If-Range` accepts nothing weaker: splicing a byte range onto a merely *equivalent* representation builds a file that never existed.

Last-Modified.description: The file's modification time as an IMF-fixdate. One-second resolution, so it is the supplementary validator; the `ETag` is the one `If-Range` is checked against.

Cache-Control.description: `no-cache` — store the response and revalidate before reusing it. Not `max-age`: a canonical file changes when the user re-runs the pipeline, which is not a schedule.

Content-Length.description: Bytes in the body: the whole artifact on a `200`, the range's length on a `206`.

X-Content-Type-Options.description: `nosniff`. The UI is served from `/` on this same origin, so a sniffed type would decide what a document *runs as*.

304.description: The client's copy is current: `If-None-Match` matched, or `If-Modified-Since` was not passed. No body, and no `Content-Length`. Returned in preference to a `206` when both a validator and a `Range` are sent — there is no point sending part of a representation the client holds all of.

416.description: The requested range is not satisfiable.

Content-Range.description: `bytes */<complete-length>` — required by RFC 9110 on a 416, and the reason the refusal is useful: the client learns the real length and can ask again.

get.summary: Search knowledge units and transcript text
get.description:
Preserves the two result shapes `query.search_knowledge` already returns, discriminated by `type` (D-028). FTS5 (T-103) replaces the linear scan behind this endpoint without changing the shapes.

A knowledge-unit hit gains `global_id` and `source_id` additively so the client can navigate; a transcript-caption hit carries no `global_id`, because v1 emits no caption entities (D-023) — it addresses its source and its timestamp instead.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query. An empty or whitespace-only query is `400 invalid_request`, not an empty result set.

parameters.name: include_transcript
parameters.description: Whether transcript captions are searched as well as knowledge units. Mirrors `include_transcript_fallback`.

200.description: A page of hits, most relevant first.

get.summary: Nodes and edges for the Knowledge Map
get.description:
`EntityRef` nodes and `IndexedRelation` edges, bounded by `limit`. Every edge states its `relation_vocabulary`, so the Map can style the two library-synthetic edge types — `derived_from` and `expresses_concept`, the most common edges in the current data — without presenting them as canonical relations.

`truncated` is stated rather than implied: a Map that has silently received part of a graph would draw a false picture of what is connected.

200.description: A bounded slice of the graph.

get.description: Nodes and edges within `depth` hops of *entity_id*, for the Map's incremental loading. The centre is echoed back so a client that batches requests cannot mis-attribute a response.

get.summary: One node per acquired source, and the relations among them
get.description:
The Source Map's topology (`T-254`). Nodes are `EntityRef` records with `entity_type: "source"` — one per acquired run, whatever its status, so a `FAIL` run is a source that exists rather than a source the Map omits.

Paged over **nodes**, exactly as `/api/graph` is: paging over relations would drop a source that relates to nothing, and a source that relates to nothing is a real source. A relation is carried when both of its endpoints are nodes of this graph and at least one of them is on this page, so a relation never names an endpoint the client has no node for.

`counts` states returned, omitted and total separately, because they answer three different questions and collapsing them is how a bounded result comes to look like a complete one.

200.description: A page of source nodes with the relations among them.

get.summary: One selected source, its readable brief and its qualified relations
get.description:
What the Source Focus composition is drawn from (`T-254`): the selected source's own `EntityRef`, its `source_knowledge` availability, and its relations split by direction with a bounded page of each one's basis.

The path parameter is the **two-part source id**, not the three-part global id of the source node; `center_id` echoes the node's global id back so a client that batches requests cannot mis-attribute a response.

`limit` bounds the relations this body carries across both directions, and `truncated` says when it bound them. A relation's basis is bounded separately by `constants.MAX_SOURCE_RELATION_BASIS`, and both `basis_total` and `basis_returned` are stated, so a truncated basis is never presented as the whole of it.

200.description: The selected source and its qualified relations.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous `page.next_cursor`. Opaque on purpose: the encoding belongs to the index (T-007), and a client that parses it has coupled itself to a private detail. A cursor the server cannot read is `400 invalid_request`.

SourceIdPath.name: source_id
SourceIdPath.description: Two-part source id, `<source_type>:<external_id>`. A colon is a legal path character (RFC 3986 `pchar`) and needs no escaping. Resolved through `pipeline.resolve_run_dir`, which rejects rather than sanitises (D-020).

ArtifactIdPath.name: artifact_id
ArtifactIdPath.description: Three-part global id of an artifact, e.g. `youtube:pqlWNihgdjI:transcript`.

RunStatusQuery.name: status
RunStatusQuery.description: Filter on the copied validation status. `UNKNOWN` is selectable, so a run with a missing validator file can be found rather than disappearing.

ProvenanceClassQuery.name: provenance_class
ProvenanceClassQuery.description: Filter on origin: source evidence, recorded synthesis, or user content.

MinConfidenceQuery.name: min_confidence
MinConfidenceQuery.description: Keep only entities whose copied confidence is at least this value. An entity with a null confidence is excluded, because no canonical file states a number for it and a default would be invented.

RelationVocabularyQuery.name: relation_vocabulary
RelationVocabularyQuery.description: Filter on which of the three edge vocabularies an edge belongs to.

ApiVersion.description: The API surface version. Fixed for the life of `schemas/api/v1/`. A breaking change becomes `schemas/api/v2/` and a `/api/v2/` path prefix, leaving these paths answering v1 (D-026).

PageInfo.description: Where a page sits in a collection.

next_cursor.description: Token for the next page, or null at the end of the collection.

total.description: Total matching records, or null when the server did not count them. Null means unknown — it never means zero.

ErrorCode.description: Closed error vocabulary. `invalid_id` is D-020 surfaced over HTTP: an id that fails `ids.py` or `resolve_run_dir` is refused before anything is read, and is reported as malformed rather than as absent. `unavailable` is the honest answer for an artifact whose record exists but whose file does not — the alternative, a placeholder, is forbidden by canvas plan §15.

message.description: Human-readable, and safe to show. It names what was wrong with the request, never a host path.

detail.description: Structured context, or null. Never carries an absolute host path (risk R15).

IndexState.description: What the index can answer with. `absent` and `building` are reported plainly: a UI that cannot tell an empty index from an unbuilt one will present 'no sources' as a fact.

RunStatusTally.description: Sources per copied status. Counting is the only operation performed on a status.

SkippedRun.description: A run directory the index scanned and could not turn into a `Source`. It is named rather than counted so that a `counts.sources` smaller than `runs.discovered` never has to be explained by guesswork.

relative_path.description: The run directory, relative to the project root.

reason.description: Why the run could not be indexed, in the words of whatever refused it. Never a host path (D-030).

built_at.description: When the index last finished a build, or null if it never has.
built_at.$comment: The `oneOf` mirrors `Source.imported_at`, which refers to `common.schema.json#/$defs/isoTimestamp` and is correctly rejected for `"yesterday"`. This field carried `format: date-time` and no pattern, and `isoTimestamp`'s own `$comment` explains why that is not a check: `format` is annotation-only in 2020-12 unless a validator opts into the format-assertion vocabulary, and none of this repo's validators do. So `built_at: "yesterday"` validated against every check in the tree while the identical value on `imported_at` did not.

index_version.description: Migration version of the SQLite schema (T-101), or null when no index exists.

message.description: Why the index is in this state, when it has something to say. Present on `error`; on `ready` after a scan that failed and was rolled back — the stored records are intact and still answerable, and this is the only place that says the last scan did not finish; and on `ready` when the index holds sources whose searchable text could not be read, which is why a search over them reports `total: null`. Such a source is *indexed*, so it is counted in `runs.indexed` and named in no `skipped` entry, and this sentence is the only channel that explains the uncountable total. The count, not the ids: `/api/sources` is where a client learns which source is which. Absent when there is nothing to report; never an empty string. Carries no host filesystem path (ADR 0003).

counts.description: Records the index holds. A cache convenience, reproducible from the canonical files; a stale count is a bug, never a data achievement.

adapters.description: The registered adapters, so a stale record can be traced to the code that wrote it.

runs.description: What the last scan saw on disk, and what it could not index. `discovered` counts run directories holding a `metadata.json`; `indexed` counts those that produced a `Source`. Every other one is named in `skipped`, so a library that is smaller than the filesystem says why rather than simply being smaller. `discovered` equals `indexed` plus the length of `skipped`. A run indexed *with* named gaps counts as indexed and reports those gaps on its own `Source.adapter_metadata`. Optional: an implementation that scans no filesystem omits it rather than reporting a zero it did not measure.

library_skipped_reason.description: Why the cross-source `library/` fragment could not be indexed, when it could not be. It is **not** a run: it is not counted in `discovered` or `indexed` and is not listed in `skipped`, so the identity above stays true — it gets a field of its own for the same reason `ScanReport.library_skipped_reason` does, so a caller can test it without matching on a path. Absent when the fragment indexed cleanly *and* when there is no fragment at all: an absent `library/` is the ordinary state of a project that has not run `rebuild-library`, while a present unreadable one is damage and says so. Carries no host filesystem path (ADR 0003).

SearchHitKnowledgeUnit.description: A knowledge-unit hit, field for field as `query.search_knowledge` returns it, plus `global_id` and `source_id`. The canonical field names are kept — `video_id` stays `video_id` (ADR 0001 invariant 6) and `id` stays the canonical unit id — so the shape the MCP tools and the CLI already return is the shape the API returns.

id.description: The canonical knowledge unit id, e.g. `KU-000001`.

start_sec.description: Present only when the canonical unit states a numeric start. Absent, not zero, when it does not.

source_url.description: Deep link built by `io.timestamp_url`. Present only alongside `start_sec`.

derived_from.description: Present only for a derived-class unit, in the canonical id form the unit itself carries.

global_id.description: Additive. Null when the canonical data cannot form one — a run whose metadata states no `video_id` has no addressable entity, and a fabricated id would be worse than none.

SearchHitTranscriptCaption.description: A transcript-caption hit, field for field as `query.search_knowledge` returns it, plus `source_id`. It carries no `global_id`: v1 emits no caption entities (D-023), so there is no entity to address. The client navigates by source and timestamp instead.

query.description: The query as executed, echoed so a client batching requests cannot mis-attribute a response.

edges.description: The relations among the nodes on this page, at most `maxItems` of them. `limit` bounds the *nodes*, and an edge list is quadratic in the nodes it connects, so the two are not the same size; `truncated` is true when either was cut.

truncated.description: True when `limit` cut the result short. Stated rather than implied, so the Map never presents a partial graph as the whole one.

edges.description: The relations among the nodes on this page, at most `maxItems` of them. `limit` bounds the *nodes*, and an edge list is quadratic in the nodes it connects, so the two are not the same size; `truncated` is true when either was cut.

SourceKnowledgeAvailability.description: Whether a source's readable brief is available, and why not when it is not. A brief is a gated derived artifact that may simply not have been generated yet, and an absent one must not reach the client as an empty successful brief — 'this source has no thesis and no key points' is a claim about the source, and it would be false. `state` carries the distinction and `brief` is null whenever the state is `unavailable`. `stale` is its own state rather than an error: the brief exists and describes inputs whose digests have since moved, so it is carried with that said out loud rather than withheld or silently trusted — `stale` is the one state other than `available` in which `brief` is a document. (`T-254` sharpened these two sentences, which had frozen in contradiction with each other: the first said a brief is null in every state but `available`, the second that a stale one is shown rather than withheld. Serving it is what makes `stale` differ from `unavailable` by more than a word.)

brief.description: The generated brief, or null when there is not one to show.

reason.description: Why the brief is unavailable or stale, project-relative and free of host paths (D-030, D-051). Null when `state` is `available`.

SourceRelationSummary.description: One source relation as the Source Explore graph needs it: direction, type, scope and how many grounds stand behind it — but not the grounds themselves. `basis_total` is required here precisely because the basis is absent: an edge pill reads `critiques · 3 grounds`, and a summary that omitted the count would let a relation resting on one pair and one resting on forty draw identically. The count is a count, never a strength, a confidence or a rank (D-247).

provenance_class.description: Always `derived` for an automatic source relation.

basis_total.description: How many knowledge-unit pairs the stored relation rests on.

SourceRelationDetail.description: One source relation with its Persian rationale and a bounded page of its basis. The two counts are both required and are not the same number: `basis_total` is what the canonical record holds, `basis_returned` is what is in this body. A response that carried only the second would present a truncated basis as the whole of it, which is the overclaim risk R27 names, arriving through the API instead of through the model. `basis` is capped at `maxItems`, the value of constants.MAX_SOURCE_RELATION_BASIS, for the reason `GraphPayload.edges` is capped: an unbounded array in a response is an unbounded response.

basis.description: The grounds carried in this body, in the stored order. Mixed and contrary grounds are included rather than filtered: hiding them would make the relation read cleaner than the evidence is.

SourceGraphPayload.description: The source topology: one node per acquired source, and the relations among them. The nodes are `EntityRef` records with `entity_type: "source"` — the same addressable handle every other entity uses, so a source selection resolves the way a knowledge unit selection does. Chapters, posts in a self-thread, transcript segments, knowledge units and concepts are not nodes here; that is the whole point of the second Map mode (D-244).

truncated.description: True when `limit` cut the result short. Stated rather than implied, exactly as `GraphPayload.truncated` is.

SourceGraphCounts.description: Returned, omitted and total, counted separately. Three numbers rather than one because they answer three different questions, and collapsing them is how a bounded result comes to look like a complete one. `sources_total` may be null, which means not counted — never zero, the same rule `PageInfo.total` carries.

relations_omitted.description: Relations the bound left out of this body. Counted, never silent — the same discipline the synthesis file's `candidates.omitted` carries upstream.

SourceNeighborhoodPayload.description: One selected source, its readable brief, and its qualified relations in both directions. `incoming` and `outgoing` are separate arrays rather than one list with a direction flag, because direction is what the Focus composition places on the left and the right and what the semantic companion list has to state in text — and a client that has to derive it by comparing `to_source_id` with `center_id` is a client that can derive it wrongly.

source.description: The selected source's own `EntityRef`, echoed back.

incoming.description: Relations whose `to_source_id` is the selected source.

outgoing.description: Relations whose `from_source_id` is the selected source.

neighbors.description: The `EntityRef` of every source named by a returned relation, so no relation names an endpoint the client has no node for. ADR 0002 is emphatic that an edge to a node the page will not show asserts a node that does not exist.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed: a rejected id (`invalid_id`), or a bad parameter or unreadable cursor (`invalid_request`).

IndexUnavailable.description: The index is absent, building, or in error, so no honest answer can be given yet (`index_unavailable`).

InternalError.description: The server could not complete the request (`internal`). Declared because the handler that produces it exists: any unforeseen failure is rendered in this envelope rather than as a framework traceback, and a contract that does not say so is a contract a client cannot hold the server to.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists and does not answer this method (`invalid_request`). v1 is read-only, so every method but `GET` and `HEAD` is refused here; the response carries `Allow` naming what the path does accept, as RFC 9110 requires. Declared for the same reason `500` is: the router produces it, and a contract that does not say so is a contract a client cannot hold the server to.

NotFound.description: The id is well-formed but names nothing (`not_found`), or names an artifact whose file is absent (`unavailable`).
